title: UNIT 5: THE HUMAN BODY SYSTEMS
notes: ✓ The human body consists of interconnected organ systems that work together to maintain life.

title: 5.1 HUMAN MUSCULOSKELETAL SYSTEMS
notes:
✓ The musculoskeletal system provides movement, body shape, support and protection.

✓ Components:
◆ Bones
◆ Muscles
◆ Cartilage
◆ Tendons
◆ Ligaments
◆ Joints
◆ Connective tissues

→ Tendon connects muscle to bone.
→ Ligament connects bone to bone.
→ Cartilage reduces friction between bones.
→ Bone marrow produces blood cells.
→ Bones store minerals, especially calcium.

title: 5.1.1 TYPES OF MUSCLES
notes:
✓ There are three major muscle types:

◆ Cardiac muscle → involuntary, striated; found only in the heart; pumps blood. Cells have intercalated discs.

◆ Skeletal muscle → voluntary, striated; attached to bones; produces body movement. A group controlled by one motor axon forms a motor unit.

◆ Smooth muscle → involuntary, non-striated; found in walls of organs such as stomach, intestine, bladder, uterus and blood vessels.

title: 5.1.2 MECHANISM OF ACTION OF SKELETAL MUSCLES
notes:
✓ Muscle contraction occurs when actin and myosin filaments slide past each other.

◆ Sarcomere → basic contractile unit.
◆ Actin → thin filament.
◆ Myosin → thick filament and molecular motor.
◆ ATP → supplies energy.
◆ Troponin → regulatory protein complex.
◆ Tropomyosin → blocks myosin-binding sites when relaxed.

→ Sequence: nerve impulse → Ca²⁺ release → Ca²⁺ binds troponin → actin-myosin cross-bridges → ATP-powered contraction → Ca²⁺ returns to sarcoplasmic reticulum → relaxation.

title: TYPES OF MUSCLE CONTRACTION
notes:
◆ Isometric → muscle tension increases but muscle length stays the same.
◆ Concentric → muscle shortens while contracting.
◆ Eccentric → muscle lengthens while contracting.

✓ Muscle contraction depends on sliding of thin actin and thick myosin filaments.

title: 5.1.3 HUMAN AXIAL & APPENDICULAR SKELETONS
notes:
✓ An adult human skeleton normally has 206 bones.

◆ Axial skeleton = 80 bones → skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum; mainly supports and protects the body.
◆ Appendicular skeleton = 126 bones → shoulder girdles, pelvis, arms, legs, hands and feet; mainly involved in movement.

✓ Bone cells:
◆ Osteoblasts → build bone
◆ Osteocytes → mature bone cells
◆ Osteoclasts → break down bone
◆ Osteoprogenitor cells → help bone repair

→ Bone strength comes mainly from collagen + calcium phosphate.

title: TYPES OF BONES
notes:
✓ Based on shape:

◆ Long bones → femur, humerus
◆ Short bones → wrist and ankle bones
◆ Flat bones → skull, ribs, sternum
◆ Irregular bones → vertebrae and other complex-shaped bones

✓ Bones provide support, protection, movement, mineral storage and blood-cell production.

title: 5.1.4 JOINTS
notes:
✓ A joint is the place where two or more bones meet. Joints allow movement and provide stability.

◆ Ball-and-socket → movement in many directions; shoulder, hip.
◆ Hinge → movement mainly in one plane; elbow, knee.
◆ Condyloid → movement without rotation; fingers, jaw.
◆ Pivot → rotational movement; neck.
◆ Gliding → bones slide over each other; wrist.
◆ Saddle → back-and-forth and side-to-side movement; thumb.

title: 5.2 THE REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM
notes:
✓ The reproductive system produces gametes and enables reproduction.

◆ Male → produces and deposits sperm.
◆ Female → produces eggs and provides the site for fertilization and fetal development.
→ Fertilization → fusion of sperm and egg to form a zygote.

title: 5.2.1 MALE REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM
notes:
◆ Testes → produce sperm + testosterone.
◆ Seminiferous tubules → sperm production.
◆ Epididymis → sperm maturation and storage.
◆ Vas deferens → carries sperm.
◆ Seminal vesicles → add fructose-rich fluid to semen.
◆ Prostate gland → adds alkaline fluid that helps protect sperm.
◆ Cowper's gland → secretes mucus-rich fluid.
◆ Urethra → carries urine and semen.
◆ Penis → deposits sperm during ejaculation.
◆ Scrotum → protects testes and regulates their temperature.

title: 5.2.1 FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM
notes:
◆ Ovaries → produce eggs + estrogen and other hormones.
◆ Fallopian tubes → carry ovum; usual site of fertilization.
◆ Uterus → site of embryo/fetal development.
◆ Endometrium → inner uterine lining for implantation.
◆ Cervix → lower opening of uterus.
◆ Vagina → birth canal and passage to outside.
◆ Labia majora/minora → protect external reproductive structures.
◆ Bartholin's glands → produce lubricating mucus.
◆ Clitoris → sensitive external reproductive organ.

title: 5.2.2 GAMETOGENESIS
notes:
✓ Gametogenesis = formation of haploid gametes.

◆ Spermatogenesis → sperm formation in seminiferous tubules.
→ PGC → spermatogonium → primary spermatocyte → secondary spermatocytes → spermatids → spermatozoa.
→ One primary spermatocyte ultimately produces four sperm cells.

◆ Oogenesis → egg formation in ovaries.
→ Oogonium → primary oocyte → secondary oocyte/ovum + polar bodies.

◆ Spermiogenesis = transformation of spermatids into mature spermatozoa.

title: 5.2.2 MENSTRUAL CYCLE
notes:
✓ The menstrual cycle prepares the female reproductive system for pregnancy. Average cycle ≈ 28 days, but normal variation occurs.

◆ Follicular phase → follicle develops; FSH is important.

◆ Ovulation → LH surge releases the secondary oocyte.

◆ Luteal phase → corpus luteum produces progesterone; endometrium is maintained.

→ Menstruation → if fertilization does not occur, hormone levels fall and the uterine lining is shed.

title: POSITIVE & NEGATIVE FEEDBACK IN MENSTRUAL CYCLE
notes:
→ Positive feedback → rising estrogen stimulates an LH surge → ovulation.

→ Negative feedback → progesterone and estrogen suppress FSH/LH → prevents development of additional follicles.

→ If fertilization fails → corpus luteum degenerates → estrogen/progesterone decrease → endometrium breaks down → menstruation.

title: 5.2.3 FERTILIZATION & PREGNANCY
notes:
✓ Fertilization → sperm + egg fuse in the ampulla of the fallopian tube → zygote.

→ Zygote → repeatedly divides while moving toward uterus.

→ Implantation → embryo attaches to endometrium, beginning about 6 days after fertilization.

◆ Pregnancy/gestation → fetal development in uterus; about 40 weeks.
◆ Multiple pregnancy → more than one fetus.

◆ Common signs: missed period, tender breasts, nausea/vomiting, increased hunger and frequent urination.

title: 5.2.4 MECHANISM OF ACTION OF CONTRACEPTIVES
notes:
✓ Contraception = intentional prevention of pregnancy.

◆ Barrier methods → physically prevent sperm from reaching egg: male/female condoms, diaphragm, cervical cap.
◆ Chemical methods → spermicides kill or disable sperm.
◆ Hormonal methods → prevent ovulation and/or thicken cervical mucus.
◆ IUD → interferes with fertilization and implantation.
◆ Implant/injection → release hormones to prevent ovulation.
◆ Sterilization → permanently prevents fertilization.

→ Condoms also provide protection against STIs.

title: CONTRACEPTIVE TYPES & TERMS
notes:
◆ Spermicides → sperm-killing chemicals.
◆ COC → combined oral contraceptive containing estrogen + progesterone.
◆ POP → progesterone-only pill.
◆ IUD → intrauterine device.
◆ Implant → hormone-releasing rod placed under skin.
◆ Injection → hormonal contraceptive such as Depo-Provera.
◆ Emergency/post pill → emergency hormonal contraception.
◆ Contraceptive ring → hormone-releasing vaginal ring.
◆ Tubal ligation → blocks fallopian tubes.
◆ Vasectomy → blocks vas deferens.

title: 5.2.5 CAUSES OF INFERTILITY IN HUMANS
notes:
✓ Infertility = inability to reproduce naturally.

◆ Female causes: ovulation problems, thyroid disorders, damaged fallopian tubes, cervical mucus problems, fibroids and endometriosis.

◆ Male causes: low sperm production, abnormal sperm function, blocked sperm ducts, varicocele, undescended testes, hypogonadism, infections and systemic diseases.

title: 5.2.6 MAJOR STIs IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
✓ STIs = communicable infections mainly transmitted through sexual contact. Major pathogens include bacteria, viruses and parasites.

✓ Important examples:
◆ Bacterial vaginosis
◆ Chlamydia
◆ Syphilis
◆ Gonorrhea
◆ Genital herpes
◆ Genital warts/HPV
◆ HIV/AIDS
◆ Hepatitis B
◆ Trichomoniasis
◆ Pubic lice
◆ Scabies
◆ Molluscum contagiosum

→ Prevention includes safer sexual practices, correct condom use, testing, treatment and avoiding shared contaminated needles.

title: BACTERIAL STIs
notes:
◆ Chlamydia → caused by Chlamydia trachomatis; may cause abnormal discharge, pain and infertility if untreated.

◆ Syphilis → caused by Treponema pallidum; stages include primary, secondary, latent and tertiary.

◆ Gonorrhea → bacterial infection that commonly affects reproductive and urinary tracts.

◆ Bacterial vaginosis → bacterial imbalance associated with abnormal vaginal discharge and odor.

title: VIRAL & PARASITIC STIs
notes:
◆ HIV → attacks CD4/T-helper cells and weakens immunity.
◆ Hepatitis B → viral infection that damages the liver.
◆ Genital herpes → caused by herpes simplex virus; produces genital sores/blisters.
◆ Genital warts → commonly associated with HPV.
◆ Trichomoniasis → caused by Trichomonas vaginalis.
◆ Pubic lice → parasitic infestation spread by close/sexual contact.
◆ Scabies → caused by mites and spreads through skin contact.

title: HIV/AIDS
notes:
✓ HIV = Human Immunodeficiency Virus; a retrovirus that attacks CD4 helper T cells.

◆ Acute infection → early stage; flu-like symptoms may occur.
◆ Chronic infection → virus remains active; may have few symptoms.
◆ AIDS → severe immune-system damage; opportunistic infections become common.

◆ AIDS = Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.
◆ CD4 cells = important immune cells.
◆ Opportunistic infection = infection taking advantage of weakened immunity.
◆ Capsid = viral core containing RNA.
◆ Envelope = outer viral covering.
◆ Glycoproteins = surface proteins used in viral attachment.

title: 5.2.8 EPIDEMIOLOGY OF STIs IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
✓ Epidemiology = study of disease occurrence, transmission, causes, outbreaks, surveillance and control.

→ STI epidemiology examines their causes, transmission, distribution and prevention.

✓ Major risk factors:
◆ Unprotected/inconsistent condom use
◆ Multiple sexual partners
◆ Previous STI
◆ Sexual violence
◆ Alcohol/recreational drug misuse
◆ Shared injection needles
◆ Young age

→ Prevention includes testing, treatment, safer sex and health education.

title: 5.5.1 EFFECTS OF ALCOHOL USE
notes:
✓ Excessive alcohol use can cause:

◆ Confusion and sleepiness
◆ Brain damage and nutritional deficiencies
◆ Liver damage/cirrhosis
◆ Cancer risk
◆ Violence and accidents
◆ Coma and death at very high levels
◆ Risky sexual behavior
◆ Increased HIV/STI transmission risk

→ Chronic heavy use can seriously damage body systems.

title: 5.5.2 EFFECTS OF CHEWING KHAT
notes:
✓ Khat = Catha edulis; its leaves contain the stimulant cathinone, which stimulates the central nervous system.

✓ Possible effects:
◆ Hypertension
◆ Stomatitis, esophagitis and gastritis
◆ Constipation
◆ Acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction
◆ Diabetes and metabolic disorders
◆ Hepatitis and liver cirrhosis

→ Cathinone is the major psychoactive stimulant in khat.

title: 5.5.3 EFFECTS OF DRUG USE
notes:
✓ Important drugs discussed include cannabis/marijuana, cocaine, heroin and inhalants.

◆ Cannabis → affects brain function, memory and judgment.
◆ Cocaine → powerful stimulant; increases cardiovascular and behavioral risks.
◆ Heroin → highly addictive opioid made from morphine.
◆ Inhalants → chemicals inhaled for psychoactive effects.

title: KEY TERMS TO REMEMBER
notes:
◆ Musculoskeletal → bones + muscles + supporting tissues.

◆ Tendon → muscle-to-bone connection.

◆ Ligament → bone-to-bone connection.

◆ Sarcomere → contractile unit of muscle.

◆ Actin → thin muscle filament.

◆ Myosin → thick muscle filament.

◆ Gametogenesis → gamete formation.

◆ Spermatogenesis → sperm formation.

◆ Oogenesis → egg formation.

◆ Ovulation → release of secondary oocyte.

◆ Fertilization → fusion of sperm and egg.

◆ Zygote → first cell formed after fertilization.

◆ Implantation → embryo attaches to uterine lining.

◆ Gestation → pregnancy period.

◆ Infertility → inability to reproduce naturally.

◆ STI → sexually transmitted infection.

◆ Epidemiology → study of disease distribution and transmission.

◆ Contraception → prevention of pregnancy.

◆ Family planning → planning number, timing and spacing of children.

◆ FGM → partial/total removal of external female genital organs.

◆ HIV → Human Immunodeficiency Virus.

◆ AIDS → Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.

◆ CD4 → immune cells targeted by HIV.
